octen.snippet:
Alamo Group Inc. (NYSE: ALG) reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $403.1 million, down 4.0% from $420.0 million a year earlier, as a $33.3 million net pretax charge tied to portfolio optimization pushed GAAP diluted EPS to $0.17 from $2.10. Adjusted diluted EPS, which excludes the charges, was $2.06 versus $2.34 in the prior-year quarter.
Divestitures and Acquisition Reshape the Portfolio
During the quarter, the Seguin, Texas-based equipment maker substantially completed planned portfolio optimization initiatives aimed at improving long-term margins, particularly in its Vegetation Management Division. The actions included the sale and wind-down of certain businesses and product lines, including Dixie Chopper and Boxer, and resulted in $33.3 million of net pretax charges.
Of those charges, $7.3 million reduced sales, $15.5 million was recorded in cost of sales, $9.0 million in selling, general and administrative expenses and $1.5 million in other income and expense. The divestiture actions also produced discrete tax impacts that temporarily raised the quarterly effective tax rate, the company said, while its underlying rate remained generally consistent with historical levels.
Separately, on October 27, 2026, Alamo acquired 100% of U.K. roadway maintenance vocational truck maker Econ Engineering Group Limited for £120.0 million ($158.7 million), plus customary closing adjustments, using borrowings under its revolving credit facility.
